prop: This memo was written against tetel commit b490574800815c1485848a92d2d10d3f27434ecc; every citation into source is to that tree.

At this pin, provenance is a byte-equality test over the whole re-rendered document: snapshot::check renders the snapshot directory with the current compose::render and returns Matches only on exact equality with the memo's bytes, Drifted otherwise. Its four outcomes (Missing, Matches, Drifted, Unreadable) carry nothing saying which of the three inputs — the document, the snapshot, or the renderer — changed.

The ticket's class reproduces at this pin: a build differing from it by one appended line in compose::render, with no committed memo touched, reports [provenance-drift] and exits 1 on the tet28 and tet29 memos, which the unmodified build checks with exit 0. Its message attributes the drift to a hand edit or an un-re-rendered workspace and names no renderer change.

A renderer change reddens CI in this repository, not only a local check: tests/check_cli.rs runs the built binary's `check` on the committed tet28 and tet29 memos and asserts exit 0, and provenance drift is a failing machine row, so the test fails under `cargo test --all-targets` until both memos re-render byte-for-byte under the new renderer.

Comparing only author-controlled text (the ticket's option 2) would leave graded evidence unguarded: `check` takes the claims it grades by parsing the rendered ledger table out of the document, every proposition_digest on record was computed over that rendered ledger cell, and it also parses the rendered target rows and transplant premises. All of these sections are generated by render rather than written by the author, so excluding them from provenance would let a hand edit to them change what `check` grades without any provenance finding.

Re-rendering a committed memo does not need its authoring workspace: snapshot::check already renders from the <memo>.tetel directory alone, and the 12 committed memos all re-render byte-for-byte from their snapshots at this pin. The workspaces exist only in a per-machine state directory outside the repository, so a remedy that needs them — which is what the drift message's "re-render" means today — is unavailable on a fresh clone or a CI runner.

Re-rendering is not free of side effects on grading: because proposition digests are computed over the rendered ledger cell, a renderer change that alters how a claim's proposition is written into the ledger (for example compose::ledger_cell's escaping or newline handling) changes the digest of that claim on re-render, and every record graded against the old digest stops matching it. A remedy that re-renders must detect this case, not assume it away.

Decision: `render --out` also writes a render record, <memo>.tetel/render.json, holding the sha256 of the document bytes it wrote, a map from each SNAPSHOT_FILES name present in the snapshot to that file's sha256, and buildid::label(). The record is written inside snapshot::write, which takes the rendered bytes as a new argument, so both of its two callers get it and neither can forget it. It is written only after compose::render over the just-copied snapshot directory reproduces those bytes exactly. The two render --out paths render and copy in two separate reads of the workspace, so without that re-render the record could certify a pair that never matched.

Decision: when the re-render differs from the document, snapshot::check consults the render record and returns one of four outcomes in place of today's single Drifted. No record: Unattributed, today's case, with the message naming three possible causes, the renderer among them. Document sha differs from the record: DocumentEdited. A recorded file's sha differs, or a file named in the current SNAPSHOT_FILES is present but absent from the record: SnapshotEdited. Otherwise: RendererChanged, naming the build label that rendered it. The record keeps per-file digests rather than one digest over the list because SNAPSHOT_FILES has grown over time. A single digest over the current list would change the first time a name was added, and every existing snapshot would then read as SnapshotEdited.

Decision: all four non-matching outcomes stay machine failures, each with its own row kind, including RendererChanged. `check` grades an older-layout document with the current build's parsers: it takes graded claims from the rendered ledger and re-verifies the rendered target and premise sections. So a document the current renderer would not produce is one whose other verdicts this build cannot vouch for. What the ticket objects to is fixed by accurate diagnosis and a safe, one-command remedy, not by silencing the failure. The cost this keeps: a renderer change still reddens the tet28/tet29 CI test until the committed memos are re-rendered in the same change.

Decision: a new CLI-only command, `tetel rerender <memo>...`, re-renders each memo from its own <memo>.tetel directory, never from a workspace. If the re-render already matches, it writes a fresh render record and leaves the document's bytes untouched. If snapshot::check returns RendererChanged, it rewrites the document and the record. It refuses DocumentEdited and SnapshotEdited, so it can never overwrite a hand edit. It refuses Unattributed unless given `--unattributed`, which records that the operator, not the tool, vouches for the document. It refuses any memo where a claim's ledger proposition, as ledger::import reads it, would differ between the document and the re-render, naming each such claim. It is not exposed over MCP: no tool description changes.

Decision: the implementing change runs `tetel rerender` over all 12 committed memos. Each re-renders byte-for-byte at this pin, so each only gains a render record, and no byte of any memo changes. This must land before any change to render output, starting with A10 (TET-83), because a memo with no record falls under Unattributed, which rerender will not migrate unaided.

The one other consumer that assumes the document equals the current re-render is the prose-revised-since-proof line lookup: its only production call, lib.rs, prints line numbers taken from compose::block_offsets over the snapshot, which are the document's lines only when the document is what the current renderer produces. Decision: those numbers are printed as document lines only when provenance is Matches; under any other outcome the entry says the line is unknown because the document is not its snapshot's current render.

Rejected: a render-format id bumped by hand whenever render output changes (the ticket's option 1 as written). Its correctness rests on an editor remembering to bump it, and a forgotten bump makes a renderer change look like no change. Nothing existing can stand in for it: buildid::label differs between every two builds, whether or not their render output differs. The render record needs no id, because it attributes a mismatch by comparing digests of what was actually written.

Each decision is pinned by a test that goes red when the named mutation alone is applied. (i) A document X with snapshot S where render(S) differs from X, and a record holding sha(X) and S's per-file digests, is RendererChanged. Mutation: classify without reading the record, which gives Unattributed. (ii) The same state with one byte of X changed is DocumentEdited. Mutation: skip the document comparison, which gives RendererChanged. (iii) The same state with one byte of a recorded snapshot file changed is SnapshotEdited. Mutation: skip the file comparison. (iv) A record lacking a name that is absent from the snapshot is still RendererChanged, and one lacking a name that is present is SnapshotEdited. Mutation: a single digest over the current SNAPSHOT_FILES. (v) snapshot::write given bytes the copied snapshot does not re-render writes no record. Mutation: write the record unconditionally. (vi) rerender on a DocumentEdited memo leaves the document byte-identical and exits non-zero. Mutation: drop the refusal. (vii) rerender on a RendererChanged memo whose ledger proposition for one claim differs refuses and names that claim. Mutation: drop the ledger comparison. (viii) A prose-revised-since-proof entry under a non-Matches outcome prints no document line number. Mutation: always fill the line.

Decision: `render --out` also writes a render record, <memo>.tetel/render.json, holding the sha256 of the document bytes it wrote, a map from each SNAPSHOT_FILES name present in the snapshot to that file's sha256, and buildid::label(). The record is written inside snapshot::write, which takes the rendered bytes as a new argument, so both of its two callers get it and neither can forget it. snapshot::write first removes any existing render.json, then copies, then writes the new record only after compose::render over the just-copied snapshot directory reproduces those bytes exactly. The two render --out paths render and copy in two separate reads of the workspace, so without that re-render the record could certify a pair that never matched. Without the removal, a failed re-render would leave the previous record in place, and check would attribute the mismatch against a record describing an older pair.
why: Attack a1 finding 2: a failed gate left the previous render.json in place, and check would then misattribute an in-tool race as DocumentEdited.

- If certification fails, the error names the first differing line.
why: Advisor findings 1 and 2. A stale snapshot file carried forward would fail the certification of a correct render, so the snapshot must mirror the workspace. The crash window between the document write and snapshot::write read as DocumentEdited, so snapshot::write must own the document write.

prop: Decision: the implementing change adds a .gitattributes marking docs/design/** as -text. Today no .gitattributes is tracked, so a clone with core.autocrlf=true would convert the committed memos and their snapshot .jsonl files on checkout. Because SnapshotEdited is tested first, every memo would then read as a snapshot edited by hand, and rerender would refuse them all. Today the same clone gets an unattributed drift. The design would turn that into a confidently wrong attribution unless line endings are pinned.

Each test below goes red when its named mutation alone is applied.

Classification (snapshot::check):
(i) A document X with snapshot S where render(S) differs from X, and a record holding sha(X) and S's per-file digests, is RendererChanged. Mutation: classify without reading the record, which gives Unattributed.
(ii) The same state with one byte of X changed is DocumentEdited. Mutation: skip the document comparison.
(iii) The same state with one byte of a recorded snapshot file changed is SnapshotEdited. Mutation: skip the file comparison.
(iv) A record lacking a name absent from the snapshot is still RendererChanged; one lacking a name present is SnapshotEdited. Mutation: a single digest over the current SNAPSHOT_FILES.
(ix) The state of (i) with claims.jsonl deleted from the snapshot is SnapshotEdited. Mutation: walk only present files.
(xii) A matching pair beside a record whose document sha differs is StaleRecord. Mutation: skip the record on a match.
(xv) Each of Unattributed, SnapshotEdited, DocumentEdited, RendererChanged and StaleRecord makes `check` exit non-zero, under its own row kind. Mutation: report RendererChanged as a warning.

Publication (snapshot::write):
(v) Given bytes the snapshot does not re-render, it leaves no render.json, even where one existed. Mutation A: write the record unconditionally. Mutation B: drop the removal.
(xvi) A snapshot holding targets.jsonl, published from a workspace without one, ends without targets.jsonl and with a record. Mutation: the copy-only loop.
(xvii) A publication that fails at the document write, with a prior record present, leaves no render.json. Mutation: remove the record after writing the document.

rerender:
(vi) On DocumentEdited, it leaves the document byte-identical and exits non-zero. Mutation: drop the refusal.
(vii) On RendererChanged where one claim's ledger proposition differs, it refuses and names the claim. Mutation: drop the ledger comparison.
(x) On a Matches memo whose record agrees on the document sha but not on acks.jsonl, it refuses and leaves render.json byte-identical. The same holds for an edit to a facts.jsonl field render does not emit. Mutation: compare only files render never reads.
(xiii) On StaleRecord, it exits zero with a record whose document sha equals the unchanged document. Mutation: treat StaleRecord as the refusal in (x).
(xiv) With --unattributed on an Unattributed memo, it leaves a document equal to render(snapshot). Mutation: seal the existing bytes.
(xviii) It refuses Unattributed without the flag and refuses SnapshotEdited, changing no byte in either. On RendererChanged it writes render(snapshot) and a record. On a clean sealed memo it changes no byte. Mutation: any one of these branches falling through to the rewrite.

Readers:
(viii) A prose-revised-since-proof entry under a non-Matches outcome prints no document line number. Mutation: always fill the line.
(xi) Under RendererChanged, a document whose target table the current parser misreads yields no "not written by `tetel target`" row. The same misread under DocumentEdited still yields it. Mutation: run direction 2 unconditionally, which reddens the first half. Skipping it on every non-Matches outcome reddens the second.

Not pinned by a test: the backfill (C12), whose evidence is its own diff, and the .gitattributes (C16), whose evidence is `git ls-files --eol`.

prop:
Decision: when the re-render differs from the document, snapshot::check consults the render record and returns one of four outcomes in place of today's single Drifted, tested in this order:
- No record: Unattributed, today's case. The message names three possible causes, the renderer among them.
- SnapshotEdited: a recorded file's sha differs, a recorded file is missing from the snapshot, or a file named in the current SNAPSHOT_FILES is present but absent from the record. A missing file must be caught here, because rendering without it succeeds and would otherwise read as RendererChanged.
- DocumentEdited: the document's sha differs from the record.
- Otherwise: RendererChanged, naming the build label that rendered it.

When the re-render matches but a record exists whose document sha differs from the document, or whose document sha agrees while some snapshot file differs as SnapshotEdited defines it, the outcome is StaleRecord, not Matches. A matching pair beside a record of a different document means the pair was rewritten by a build that writes no record. One whose record disagrees only on files render does not read is left by such a build whenever the rewrite changed only those files, and equally by a hand edit to them; digests cannot tell the two apart. A build at or before this pin writes no record and never deletes one. StaleRecord is reported at the first check after the rewrite, while the renderer is unchanged, instead of surfacing only at the next renderer change as SnapshotEdited.

The DocumentEdited and SnapshotEdited messages each name two causes: a hand edit, or such a record-less render, since digests cannot tell them apart. The second cause is left only where a record-less render and a renderer change both happen before any check.

The record keeps per-file digests rather than one digest over the list because SNAPSHOT_FILES has grown over time. A single digest over the current list would change the first time a name was added, and every existing snapshot would then read as SnapshotEdited.
why: PR #46 review: check now fails a matching pair whose record differs only on unrendered files (StaleRecord); rerender reseals it only under a separate --reseal flag; an unreadable older ledger is refused as unreadable

prop:
Decision: a new CLI-only command, `tetel rerender <memo>...`, re-renders each memo from its own <memo>.tetel directory, never from a workspace. Every record it writes is for a document it has just made equal to the render of the snapshot, in every branch.
- Matches with a record agreeing on every digest: it changes nothing, so rerender over a clean tree is byte-idempotent.
- Matches with no record: it writes a record and leaves the document's bytes untouched.
- StaleRecord with a record agreeing on the document sha but differing on any snapshot file: it refuses and names the files unless given `--reseal`, and with it rewrites only the record. An edit that leaves the render unchanged still matches: any edit to identity.json, acks.jsonl, counters.json, pending.json or refusals.log, or one confined to facts.jsonl fields render does not emit. Resealing unasked would erase the only evidence of it. `--reseal` is not `--unattributed`: vouching for one state never consents to the other.
- StaleRecord with a record of a different document: it replaces the record and says a stale record was replaced, not that anything was edited.
- RendererChanged: it rewrites the document and the record.
- DocumentEdited and SnapshotEdited: it refuses, so it never overwrites a document or snapshot that differs from its record.
- Unattributed: it refuses unless given `--unattributed`. That flag records that the operator, not the tool, vouches for the migration. It still writes the render of the snapshot and never seals the existing bytes as they stand.
- It refuses any memo where the set of claim ids, or any claim's ledger proposition, as ledger::import reads them, would differ between the document and the re-render. It names each such claim. A document from which ledger::import reads errors, or no claims where the re-render has some, is refused as unreadable rather than reported as changed.

It is not exposed over MCP: no tool description changes.
why: PR #46 review: check now fails a matching pair whose record differs only on unrendered files (StaleRecord); rerender reseals it only under a separate --reseal flag; an unreadable older ledger is refused as unreadable

prop:
Decision: the implementing change runs `tetel rerender` over every memo in the repository that has a <memo>.tetel directory when the change is made. That is the 12 committed at this pin, plus any committed since, this memo among them. Each is expected to re-render byte-for-byte, so each only gains a render record and no byte of any memo changes. A memo that does not re-render is a finding for that change, not something to force through.

This must land before any change to render output, starting with A10 (TET-83), because a memo with no record falls under Unattributed, which rerender will not migrate unaided. A memo rewritten by a record-less build between the backfill and A10 is reported as StaleRecord at its next check, and `rerender` repairs it without a workspace, given `--reseal` where only files render does not read differ. A10 should begin by checking every memo, so that none is carried into the migration stale.
